videos.title: The Panic Is in CoreWeave's Debt. The Risk Is in AI Revenue. What Is Your Portfolio Betting On?
videos.description:
AI financing risks, index-driven buying, and opportunities beyond US tech take center stage in this week's Excess Returns Weekly Wrap. Jack Forehand and Matt Zeigler explore how investors can distinguish a stock-market setback from a financial crisis—and build portfolios that account for more than one possible future.

Featuring clips from Andy Constan, Rob Arnott, Paisley Nardini, Colin McQueen, and Brian Portnoy, the discussion connects CoreWeave's funding challenges with the broader question of whether AI can deliver on investors' expectations. It also examines the forces behind index additions, the power infrastructure AI needs, the case for international value, and why experienced investors sometimes choose cash and peace of mind over maximizing returns.

Topics covered:
- Andy Constan on why AI stocks could suffer without triggering a financial crisis
- Why the eventual return on AI spending matters for the value of today's infrastructure
- Rob Arnott's SpaceX thesis and how anticipated index buying can create opportunities
- Paisley Nardini on under-owned real assets, energy, and infrastructure investment
- Looking beyond AI labels to the businesses receiving actual spending
- Colin McQueen on international valuations, improving earnings, and catalysts for value
- Why long-term international diversification differs from protection in a market crash
- Brian Portnoy on cash reserves, career risk, and portfolios that help investors sleep at night
- Andy Constan's concerns
